items.t: Adults with type 2 diabetes, to improve glycaemic control: as monotherapy when metformin is inappropriate (contraindicated or not tolerated); as dual therapy with metformin, a sulphonylurea or a PPAR-gamma agonist; as triple therapy with a sulphonylurea plus metformin or a PPAR-gamma agonist plus metformin; and as add-on to insulin (with or without metformin).

src.q: For adult patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, Januvia is indicated to improve glycaemic control
in patients inadequately controlled by diet and exercise alone and for whom metformin is inappropriate due to contraindications or intolerance
Januvia is also indicated as add-on to insulin (with or without metformin) when diet and exercise plus stable dose of insulin do not provide adequate glycaemic control.

restrictions.note: No specialist-only, shared-care or brand-prescribing restriction found in the UK SmPC, MHRA or SPS pages checked.

items.t: 100 mg once daily. When added to metformin and/or a PPAR-gamma agonist, keep their doses unchanged.

src.q: The dose is 100 mg sitagliptin once daily.
the dose of metformin and/or PPARγ agonist should be maintained, and Januvia administered concomitantly

items.t: With a sulphonylurea or insulin: a lower dose of the sulphonylurea or insulin may be considered to reduce hypoglycaemia risk.

src.q: When Januvia is used in combination with a sulphonylurea or with insulin, a lower dose of the sulphonylurea or insulin may be considered to reduce the risk of hypoglycaemia

items.t: Renal impairment: GFR 30 to < 45 mL/min, 50 mg once daily; GFR < 30 mL/min or end-stage renal disease (including dialysis), 25 mg once daily (see Renal).

src.q: For patients with moderate renal impairment (GFR ≥ 30 to < 45 mL/min), the dose of Januvia is 50 mg once daily.
including those requiring haemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis, the dose of Januvia is 25 mg once daily

items.t: Elderly: no dose adjustment based on age.

src.q: Elderly No dose adjustment is necessary based on age.

items.t: Missed dose: take as soon as remembered; do not take a double dose on the same day.

src.q: If a dose of Januvia is missed, it should be taken as soon as the patient remembers. A double dose should not be taken on the same day.

items.t: Should not be used in children and adolescents aged 10 to 17 years (insufficient efficacy). Not studied under 10 years.

src.q: Sitagliptin should not be used in children and adolescents 10 to 17 years of age because of insufficient efficacy.
Sitagliptin has not been studied in paediatric patients under 10 years of age.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to sitagliptin or any excipient.

src.q: Contraindications Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1

items.t: Should not be used in type 1 diabetes or to treat diabetic ketoacidosis.

src.q: Januvia should not be used in patients with type 1 diabetes or for the treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis.

items.t: Acute pancreatitis: tell patients the key symptom (persistent, severe abdominal pain). If suspected, stop sitagliptin and other suspect medicines; do not restart if confirmed. Caution with a history of pancreatitis.

src.q: Patients should be informed of the characteristic symptom of acute pancreatitis: persistent, severe abdominal pain.
If pancreatitis is suspected, Januvia and other potentially suspect medicinal products should be discontinued; if acute pancreatitis is confirmed, Januvia should not be restarted.
Caution should be exercised in patients with a history of pancreatitis.

items.t: Hypoglycaemia occurs with insulin or a sulphonylurea; a lower dose of these may be considered.

src.q: Hypoglycaemia has been observed when sitagliptin was used in combination with insulin or a sulphonylurea.

items.t: Serious hypersensitivity reactions (anaphylaxis, angioedema, exfoliative skin reactions including Stevens-Johnson syndrome), usually within the first 3 months: stop sitagliptin if suspected and use another diabetes treatment.

src.q: These reactions include anaphylaxis, angioedema, and exfoliative skin conditions including Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
If a hypersensitivity reaction is suspected, Januvia should be discontinued.

items.t: Bullous pemphigoid: stop sitagliptin if suspected.

src.q: If bullous pemphigoid is suspected, Januvia should be discontinued.

items.t: When combining with another antidiabetic medicine, check that medicine's own conditions for use in renal impairment.

src.q: When considering the use of sitagliptin in combination with another anti-diabetic medicinal product, its conditions for use in patients with renal impairment should be checked.

items.t: Sulphonylureas or insulin: hypoglycaemia; a lower dose of the sulphonylurea or insulin may be considered.

src.q: Therefore, to reduce the risk of hypoglycaemia, a lower dose of sulphonylurea or insulin may be considered

items.t: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. clarithromycin, itraconazole, ketoconazole, ritonavir): could alter sitagliptin pharmacokinetics in severe renal impairment or end-stage renal disease; not assessed in a clinical study.

src.q: it is possible that potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (i.e. ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir, clarithromycin) could alter the pharmacokinetics of sitagliptin in patients with severe renal impairment or ESRD
The effect of potent CYP3A4 inhibitors in the setting of renal impairment has not been assessed in a clinical study.

items.t: Digoxin: small rise in digoxin levels; no digoxin dose change, but monitor patients at risk of digoxin toxicity.

src.q: No dose adjustment of digoxin is recommended.
patients at risk of digoxin toxicity should be monitored for this when sitagliptin and digoxin are administered concomitantly

items.t: No meaningful effect on metformin, simvastatin, warfarin or oral contraceptives in clinical studies.

src.q: sitagliptin did not meaningfully alter the pharmacokinetics of metformin, glyburide, simvastatin, rosiglitazone, warfarin, or oral contraceptives

items.t: GFR ≥ 45 mL/min (mild or moderate impairment): no dose adjustment.

src.q: For patients with mild renal impairment (glomerular filtration rate [GFR] ≥ 60 to < 90 mL/min), no dose adjustment is required.

items.t: GFR ≥ 30 to < 45 mL/min: 50 mg once daily.

src.q: For patients with moderate renal impairment (GFR ≥ 30 to < 45 mL/min), the dose of Januvia is 50 mg once daily.

items.t: GFR < 30 mL/min (severe) or end-stage renal disease (GFR < 15 mL/min), including haemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis: 25 mg once daily, given without regard to dialysis timing.

src.q: For patients with severe renal impairment (GFR ≥ 15 to <30 mL/min) or with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) (GFR < 15 mL/min), including those requiring haemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis, the dose of Januvia is 25 mg once daily.
Treatment may be administered without regard to the timing of dialysis.

items.t: Assess renal function before starting and periodically thereafter.

src.q: assessment of renal function is recommended prior to initiation of Januvia and periodically thereafter

items.t: Mild to moderate hepatic impairment: no dose adjustment.

src.q: No dose adjustment is necessary for patients with mild to moderate hepatic impairment.

items.t: Severe hepatic impairment: not studied; care should be exercised (although mainly renally eliminated).

src.q: Januvia has not been studied in patients with severe hepatic impairment and care should be exercised

items.t: SmPC: no adequate human data; animal reproductive toxicity at high doses. Should not be used in pregnancy.

src.q: There are no adequate data from the use of sitagliptin in pregnant women.
Due to lack of human data, Januvia should not be used during pregnancy.

items.t: BUMPS: type 2 diabetes in pregnancy should be treated with metformin, with insulin if needed; other antidiabetic medicines (including DPP-4 inhibitors) are avoided as a precaution. In an unplanned pregnancy, continue current treatment until reviewed promptly.

src.q: Type 2 diabetes during pregnancy should be treated with metformin, as well as insulin if required. Other antidiabetic drugs should not be used.
As a precaution, they are avoided in pregnancy.
you should carry on with the drug you are taking until your appointment, as uncontrolled diabetes is risky for you and your baby

src.q: It is unknown whether sitagliptin is excreted in human breast milk.
Januvia should not be used during breast-feeding.

items.t: SPS: insulin or metformin are the preferred choices; there is limited or no published information on other antidiabetic medicines in breastfeeding.

src.q: Insulin or metformin are the preferred choices during breastfeeding.
limited or no published information on the use of other antidiabetic (blood-glucose lowering) medicines during breastfeeding

items.t: Fertility: animal data suggest no effect; human data are lacking.

src.q: Animal data do not suggest an effect of treatment with sitagliptin on male and female fertility. Human data are lacking.
